_: TEN-242 phase 2 item C3(e). EXPLICIT mapping from the quote sheet's vocabulary
onto our TOURNAMENT_CATALOG names. Nothing here is fuzzy-matched and nothing is
inferred: a value absent from these tables FAILS LOUDLY in the import report and
the row is not imported. Adding a mapping is a deliberate act, which is the point.
`groups`   : column-1 sponsor names (the row group header) -> our catalog name.
`prefixes` : the UPPERCASE 'EVENT:' marker the quote text opens with -> our name.
These are two different vocabularies for the same events — the sheet
files under the SPONSOR name and the text names the CITY — so both
have to resolve before a conflict can be judged.
A null value means 'known, and deliberately not importable'. It carries a reason
and is reported separately from an UNKNOWN name, because 'we have no such event'
and 'nobody has mapped this yet' are different facts.

groupNotes.LAVER CUP: A team exhibition. No entry in TOURNAMENT_CATALOG and no court-speed rating, so there is no Overview page for a card to live on.
groupNotes.UNITED CUP: A mixed team event. Same reason as Laver Cup — no catalog entry, no host page.
groupNotes.NATIONAL BANK OPEN PRESENTED BY ROGERS: AMBIGUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION. The men's Canadian Open alternates between Montreal and Toronto, and our catalog carries BOTH as separate rated venues. The sponsor string names neither. Resolving it from the row's year would be an inference, and 248 of 450 rows have no year at all. Founder decision required — see the import report.
groupNotes.LIBEMA OPEN 2025: The name cell has a YEAR glued onto it, so it is not a clean group name and not a clean year cell either. The event is 's-Hertogenbosch, which we carry as `Hertogenbosch`. Left unmapped deliberately: mapping the malformed literal would hide a sheet defect that will recur.
groupNotes.MILLENNIUM ESTORIL OPEN2026: Same defect as LIBEMA, with no separating space. The event is `Estoril`, which we do carry.

prefixNotes.BRUSSELS: NOT a parse artefact and NOT a filing error. The BNP Paribas Fortis European Open moved from Antwerp to Brussels; our catalog still carries only `Antwerp`, and has no Brussels row. So the group resolves to Antwerp and the text names a city we do not model. Founder decision: is our `Antwerp` the same event, in which case these rows are fine, or does the venue move need a catalog change?
prefixNotes.AUCKLAND M: A defect in the source text: the marker reads `AUCKLAND M:`. The intent is plainly Auckland, but stripping the stray ` M` would be me editing the source. Held out and reported instead.
prefixNotes.MIAMI M: Same defect, reading `MIAMI M:`. Note this row's player cell says `Khachanov` while its text says `said Karatsev` — a separate attribution defect flagged in the report.
